### Issue Title
Improve Cloudflare Worker `postComment` metadata

### Issue Description

              @whilefoo A thing we could do for Workers is to put the url to the logs, that would look like
`https://dash.cloudflare.com/${env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/workers/services/view/${env.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME}/production/observability/logs?granularity=0&time=${timeParam}`

However this would require worker deployments to upload these values as they are not accessible through a worker by default. What do you think?

If yes, it should be its own task I believe.

_Originally posted by @gentlementlegen in https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/pull/169#discussion_r1821942110_
            

`postComment` can post the url for an Action worker, but doesn't not have context for a Worker run. What could be done is adding a url to the dashboard with the time of the run as a filter so that we instantly have the related logs displayed.

Code snippet:
```typescript
const toTime = Date.now() + 60000;
    const fromTime = Date.now() - 60000;
    const timeParam = encodeURIComponent(`{"type":"absolute","to":${toTime},"from":${fromTime}}`);

    console.log(
      `https://dash.cloudflare.com/${env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/workers/services/view/${env.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME}/production/observability/logs?granularity=0&time=${timeParam}`
    );
```

This would imply uploading `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME` during worker deployment as these values are not available by default.

To achieve this, a new reusable GitHub action could be created to avoid having to modify each upload script from every worker plugin. This would greatly benefit all the projects and make deployment simpler.

### Issue Title
Add posting to pull-request review comment capability

### Issue Description

The SDK should be able to post to pull-request threads. The API is a bit different for these as it should directly use `pull` from the REST API.

What happens right now:
- if "pull_request" is present in the payload, try to post to the pull-request itself
- if we wanted to post to the thread, we would need to use `octokit.rest.pulls.createReplyForReviewComment` or `createReviewComment`
- same thing goes for updating the comment that needs a different API
- maybe we could consider having an extra argument in the options to specify a pull-request comment ID

### Issue Title
Configuration validation and annotations on errors

### Issue Description

In the bot v1, when the configuration is changed, annotations are added to the configuration file if any error is encountered within the configuration. It would be really nice to have for v2 as it is a common scenario to have an invalid configuration and have no feedback about it because the error would only be visible within the worker logs.

The main challenge is that only plugins are aware of their configuration shape, so probably the kernel should call every plugin to check their validity, which would require an endpoint or some access to the configuration validators. At the same time, the `manifest.json` validity could be checked, relating to https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/issues/78.

Since this might imply quite a few network requests, we can also consider having this functionality as a separate Worker using [service binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/).

### Issue Description

```diff
{
```

```diff
plugins:
```

The configuration takes over the manifest is present, otherwise the manifest is the default.

### Issue Title
The command `/ask` fails on large contexts

### Issue Description

```diff
! No answer from OpenAI

<!--
{
  "caller": "issueCommentCreatedCallback"
}
-->
```
_Originally posted by @ubiquity-os-beta[bot] in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/issues/67#issuecomment-2577541987_


## What happened

The `/ask` command failed to run, due to a context being too large, thus failing with
```json
{
       "res": {
         "error": {
           "message": "Provider returned error",
           "code": 400,
           "metadata": {
             "raw": "{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"message\": \"This model's maximum context length has been exceeded. Please reduce the length of the messages.\",\n    \"type\": \"invalid_request_error\",\n    \"param\": \"messages\",\n    \"code\": \"context_length_exceeded\"\n  }\n}",
             "provider_name": "OpenAI"
           }
         },
         "user_id": "user_2njZil2BmAzm3iDZvVsx69KWg4A"
       },
       "caller": "Completions.createCompletion"
     }
```

Multiple problems here:

- it should use `postComment` so we get the run url and the proper error stack
- there should not be two comments for the failure
- the context should be truncated in some way to allow `/ask` to run properly

## What was expected

`/ask` should truncate the context so it runs properly and still gives an accurate answer.

## How to reproduce

The easiest would probably to run `/ask` against the aforementioned issue, or create an issue with a very long content.

### Issue Title
`/gpt` ask a context aware question

### Issue Description

# Overview
- Similar to an old proposal for `/ask`.
- The goal is to ask a context-aware question.
- Feed the entire conversation context into ChatGPT4o.
- Include any linked pull requests or issues and their entire conversation context.
- Prioritize the issue specification to set the topic, then add comments.
- Simplify comments by showing the username prepending the comment.
- Divide conversations in the prompt using headers and footers.

# Prompt Template

**=== Start Project Specification === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #[Issue Number] ===**
```
[GitHub issue specification body]
```
**=== End Project Specification ===**

**=== Start Issue Conversation === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #[Issue Number] ===**
```
[Comment ID] [Username]: [Comment]
[Comment ID] [Username]: [Comment]
...
```
**=== End Issue Conversation ===**

**=== Start Linked Pull Request Conversation === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #[Pull Request Number] ===**
```
[Comment ID] [Username]: [Comment]
[Comment ID] [Username]: [Comment]
...
```
**=== End Linked Pull Request Conversation ===**

**=== Start Linked Pull Request Code Diff === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #[Pull Request Number] ===**
```diff
- [Old Code]
+ [New Code]
```
**=== End Linked Pull Request Code Diff ===**

# Example

**=== Start Project Specification === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #29 ===**
```
Add a new feature to support XYZ plugins.
```
**=== End Project Specification ===**

**=== Start Issue Conversation === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #29 ===**
```
2222517181 0x4007: We should consider adding support for plugins to enhance functionality.
2222517182 rndquu: I agree, this would be beneficial.
2222517184 gentlementlegen: Do we have any specific plugins in mind?
```
**=== End Issue Conversation ===**

**=== Start Linked Pull Request Conversation === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #30 ===**
```
2222517187 devuser1: Implemented basic support for plugins.
2222517189 devuser2: This looks good, but needs more testing.
```
**=== End Linked Pull Request Conversation ===**

**=== Start Linked Pull Request Code Diff === ubiquibot/plugins-wishlist #30 ===**
```diff
- // insert log
+ console.log("test");
```
**=== End Linked Pull Request Code Diff ===**

# Notes
- Include the org/repo/issue to help ChatGPT understand references to other issues/pulls.
- Annotate comments with their IDs so that ChatGPT can produce outputs with links to other comments for references.

### Issue Title
Make this work - version one

### Issue Description

## Context

Implement a mechanism to reward contributors based on their comments by evaluating:
- **Word count** as a `quantitative` metric, focusing on content formatting.
- **Relevance** to the topic as outlined in the issue specification, marked as `qualitative`[^1].
- **Clarity** of articulation, ensuring comments are easily understandable[^2].

Exclude:
- Comments from bots.
- Bot commands, identified by syntax like `/wallet 0x...`.

Due to architectural changes, avoid generating permits in this module. Determine an appropriate return value to pass to the kernel for subsequent handling, aiming for:
1. A final permit generation interface formatted as `Record<Username, string>`, e.g., `{ "pavlovcik": "50" }`[^3].
2. Inclusion of reward amount metadata to transparently explain the rationale behind each reward[^4].

## Score Calculation

The final score is a product of the three metrics: `quantitative (sum)` * `qualitative` * `clarity`. Word counts are adjusted by element type, excluding blockquotes.

## Scope

Transition from the monolithic `ubiquibot` to a kernel-plugin structure, addressing:
- Migration and reimplementation of conversation rewards logic.
- Integration of "data aggregation" for activity related to issues and pull requests.
- Reward calculations based on `quantitative`, `qualitative`, and `clarity` evaluations.
- Display of scoring metrics in a detailed manner as in the current [reward comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/26#issuecomment-1996890295).

## Requirements

- Achieve 80%+ code coverage with Jest tests.
- Ensure scoring configurability, with initial hardcoding acceptable.
- Define the kernel-plugin interface, focusing on core logic testing independently of the kernel.
- Develop a method for returning structured data conducive to HTML table formatting by another plugin for comprehensive reward displays.

## Remarks

- Main entry point of old version. https://github.com/ubiquibot/comment-incentives/blob/main/src/handlers/issue/issue-closed.ts
- You can see I tried classifying contributor types for the sake of our config. At a high level we had four contributor main types: assignee, issuer (the issue author) collaborator (somebody added to the team) and contributor (default)
- We also need to be able to configure the scoring for all of those classes, and also, the scoring of commenting on the issue or the pull request. I think my mistake the first time around was collecting each of these individually then scoring. This time around I'm collecting everything at once, and then I think it makes sense to classify and score.


[^1]: Previous implementation used GPT-3.5 to assess how on-topic each comment is, assigning a float score accordingly.
[^2]: Clarity evaluation may involve GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 for assessing the clearness of a comment's meaning or summarizing key points from verbose contributions.
[^3]: Permit generation focuses on specifying an amount and the corresponding wallet address, without concerning itself with the underlying metadata.
[^4]: Consideration for a dedicated permit generation module that solely manages permit details to minimize the attack surface area.
